cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Harmony ≠ discord – a state of peaceful agreement and cooperation between people.

p.em: Example: Living in harmony with your roommates makes home life much more comfortable.

cosy-blockquote.p: Compassion – a strong feeling of sympathy and sadness for other people's suffering.

p.em: Example: We must show real compassion to people who have lost their homes in natural disasters.

cosy-blockquote.p: Forgiveness – the decision to stop feeling angry or resentful toward someone who hurt you.

p.em: Example: Asking for forgiveness is often the hardest part of rebuilding a friendship.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gratitude – the feeling of being thankful and showing appreciation.

p.em: Example: Keeping a journal of the things you love is a great way to practice daily gratitude.

cosy-blockquote.p: Kindness – the quality of being friendly, helpful, and caring.

p.em: Example: A simple act of kindness, like holding the door open, can brighten a stranger's day.

cosy-blockquote.p: Foster – to encourage or help something positive develop and grow.

p.em: Example: Our teacher works hard to foster a safe and supportive learning environment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gesture – an action that communicates an emotion, idea, or physical state.

p.em: Example: Offering a hot cup of tea is a simple gesture of welcome in our culture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Global – relating to the entire world; worldwide.

p.em: Example: Protecting our oceans is a global responsibility that requires every country's effort.

cosy-blockquote.p: Festival – a special day or period of celebration, often cultural or religious.

p.em: Example: The community organizing team set up a brilliant food festival in the local park.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ritual – a regular action or series of actions that you perform in a set way.

p.em: Example: Our family's Saturday morning breakfast ritual is something we never miss.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does art help us connect with others and cultivate empathy in divided communities?
★ Do you find it easy to connect with people who have different opinions?

In what ways do local festivals bring together people to share kindness?
★ When was the last time a stranger showed unexpected kindness to you?

Why is it important to reach out to neighbors and offer compassion during difficult times?
★ How do you usually support a friend who is going through a hard time?

How does volunteering help citizens get along with different members of their community?
★ Have you ever volunteered for a local project or charity?

Why do people easily bond with others when they join in a global celebration?
★ What is the most joyful celebration you have ever attended?

How can music help us bridge the gap and express affection across linguistic barriers?
★ Is there a song that always makes you feel connected to your friends?

Why does a shared meal help relatives open up to each other and achieve reconciliation?
★ How does your family resolve disagreements during holiday dinners?

How can we stand up for others to ensure a peaceful neighborhood environment?
★ Do you think your neighborhood is a peaceful place to grow up in?

What daily habits help you get along with colleagues and foster goodwill?
★ What is your secret to maintaining good relationships at work or school?

How can we reach out to younger generations to pass on the value of harmony?
★ Who taught you the most about living in harmony with others?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: 🕊️ Activity 1: The Harmony Spectrum Fostering peace requires deliberate social action. Together with your partner, evaluate these three daily avenues of connection. Rank them from 1 (most powerful catalyst for peace) to 3 (secondary/supplementary). Focus on using your phrasal verbs of connection (bond with, get along with, reach out to): 🤝 Proactive Apologies Reaching out to resolve old friction and achieve total reconciliation. 🎨 Communal Creativity Using shared neighborhood music and mural festivals to bond with diverse residents. 👵 Vulnerable Support Checking in on isolated elderly neighbors to deliver home-cooked meals and empathy. 💖 Closing: The Kindness Chain Reaction If you could trigger one effortless act of random kindness that immediately spreads across your entire city, which would you pick to implement? ☕ Free Coffee for the Person Behind You 🌸 Anonymous Handwritten Encouraging Letters 🎶 Public Musicians Playing Gentle Folk Tunes 🚌 Free Public Transit Commutes for Everyone

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, translation technology will help everyone get along with other cultures, creating universal harmony.
★ Would you miss the challenge of learning languages if instant translation was perfect?

Virtual reality platforms will bring together divided families, generating high-fidelity digital affection.
★ Can a virtual hug ever feel as meaningful as a physical one?

To prevent future conflicts, school systems will always reach out to international partners to build global goodwill.
★ Did your school have international exchange programs when you were young?

As megacities grow, local neighborhood associations will struggle to bring together a fractured community.
★ Do you know the names of the people who live next door to you?

A universal basic empathy score will determine how citizens get along with others during public celebrations.
★ Would you want your empathy levels to be measured by a computer?

Social media algorithms will be redesigned to help users bond with offline neighbors, fostering real-world empathy.
★ Do you think social media currently connects us or divides us more?

We will see the rise of digital reconciliation booths designed to help families open up to each other and achieve reconciliation.
★ Would you use an AI mediator to help resolve a family argument?

Synthetic pets will be introduced in care homes to help elderly citizens bond with active companions and experience compassion.
★ Do you think a robotic pet can offer real emotional comfort?

To ensure a peaceful future, global citizens will stand up for human rights in decentralized online assemblies.
★ What is a cause you would be willing to stand up for online?

AI companions will teach children how to reach out to lonely classmates and share kindness.
★ Do you believe children are naturally kind, or must they be taught kindness?

ul.li: Incorrect: We must to keep the peace. → Correct: We must keep the peace. ((Modal verb check: 'must' is followed by the bare infinitive 'keep' without 'to'.))
Incorrect: I make an act of kindness. → Correct: I do / perform an act of kindness. ((Collocation: 'acts of kindness' are typically 'done' or 'performed', not 'made'.))
Incorrect: I am full of gratitude for you. → Correct: I am full of gratitude to you / towards you. ((Preposition check: we feel/show gratitude 'to' or 'towards' a person for something they did.))
